question.problem:
The function $f(x)$ is defined for every real number $x$ and is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{cx+4}, & x\ne -1, \\ \frac{1}{27}, & x=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=-1,$ what is the value of $c?$
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -1}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{cx+4}={(\frac{1}{3})}^{4-c}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-1,$ we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}f(x) & =f(-1) \\ {(\frac{1}{3})}^{4-c} & =\frac{1}{27} \\ {(\frac{1}{3})}^{4-c} & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{3} \\ 4-c & =3 \\ c & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
